statement: openLB implements the Shan-Chen multiphase model as a coupling between two partner lattices (one per component): a post-processor computes a common velocity shared by both populations and an interaction force from a lattice-stencil sum of the interaction potential, stored as external force on each lattice.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - two-lattice Shan-Chen with per-component density normalization (force divided by own density) is the baseline industrial pattern for phase-separation/free-surface-adjacent studies.
TensorLBM service: reference design for a multiphase coupling layer (common velocity + force injection) to benchmark TensorLBM's own multiphase scheme against.

statement: openLB provides a pluggable library of interaction potentials as AnalyticalF1D functors - ShanChen93, ShanChen94, PengRobinson, CarnahanStarling, Krause, WeisbrodKrause, Normal and PsiEqualsRho - so the equation of state is swapped without touching collision code.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - a swappable EOS/potential library behind one interface is an industrial-grade engineering pattern (configuration, not code fork).
TensorLBM service: adopt a pluggable interaction-potential interface so EOS selection becomes a configuration choice.

statement: The PengRobinson and CarnahanStarling interaction potentials provide a second operator() overload that accepts a temperature field, enabling temperature-dependent (thermally coupled) multiphase simulations.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - a temperature-dependent EOS is the minimal hook for thermally coupled multiphase (evaporating/condensing interfaces, boiling-adjacent flows).
TensorLBM service: if TensorLBM adds multiphase, design the potential interface to accept an optional temperature field from day one.

statement: openLB implements a multi-component free-energy model: one density lattice per component coupled through a chemical potential whose gradient is evaluated with a 9-point (1/12) stencil; the coupling supports two or three components (partners.size() > 1).
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - the free-energy model with chemical-potential coupling is the route to thermodynamically consistent surface tension (Young-Laplace validation example ships in-repo).
TensorLBM service: the 9-point 1/12 gradient stencil for the chemical potential is a concrete, testable pattern for gradient-based multiphase coupling.

statement: The Boussinesq thermal-coupling post-processor applies a body force proportional to the temperature difference (force = gravity*dir*(T-T0)) on the velocity lattice and copies the velocity from the temperature lattice for the advection term.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - Boussinesq coupling is the standard industrial pattern for natural convection (Rayleigh-Benard, cooling, HVAC).
TensorLBM service: force = gravity*dir*(T-T0) plus velocity-copy is a minimal, testable thermal-coupling contract to mirror in TensorLBM.

statement: The temperature field is carried on a separate D3Q7 advection-diffusion lattice (7 directions), and the Navier-Stokes lattice reads its velocity field for the advection term.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - a dedicated low-direction (D3Q7) thermal lattice keeps thermal advection cheap while the velocity lattice keeps full accuracy.
TensorLBM service: consider a reduced-direction thermal lattice to cut thermal-simulation cost on large meshes.

notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - an in-repo validation surface (analytical reference printed beside the numeric) is the industrial-grade habit TensorLBM should copy.
TensorLBM service: port the 'print numerical vs analytical side by side' pattern into TensorLBM validation examples; magnitudes must be re-run before reuse since the snapshot bundles no results.

statement: openLB's descriptor system is a variadic template (DESCRIPTOR_BASE<D,Q,FIELDS...>) with compile-time field introspection (provides/index/size), enabling compile-time-checked field access across dynamics, boundaries and functors.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - compile-time field introspection is how openLB keeps one codebase across BGK/MRT/porous/particle dynamics without runtime branching.
TensorLBM service: a descriptor/field-tag system with compile-time checks would prevent field-mismatch bugs in TensorLBM multi-physics coupling.

statement: In openLB, bounce-back is implemented as a Dynamics class (not a boundary condition) with an optional fictitious density; off-boundary conditions live in the boundary module.
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - modeling bounce-back as a dynamics (with fictitious-density option) localizes wall behavior and keeps the boundary module thin.
TensorLBM service: compare against TensorLBM's boundary design; the fictitious-density constructor is a useful knob for multiphase walls.

statement: openLB ships Smagorinsky, dynamic Smagorinsky and WALE subgrid-scale models (plus porous-media variants) for industrial turbulence, with the turbulent relaxation time added to the molecular one (tau_eff = tau_mol + tau_turb).
notes: GAP anchor: GAP-LBM-INDUSTRIAL-ENG - Smagorinsky/dynamic/WALE with tau_eff = tau_mol + tau_turb is the industrial turbulence baseline for LBM CFD.
TensorLBM service: for industrial CFD targets, a WALE option (rotation-aware) is the differentiator over plain Smagorinsky.
